subject.title: Durable Core PR 5/6: add operation-scoped execution recovery

question: Should OpenClaw adopt a core, opt-in cross-owner durable recovery layer with authority-mode startup and replay-fencing behavior, or require the identified recovery gaps to stay within existing task, session, subagent, and delivery owners?
rationale: This is an architectural and compatibility contract choice: the patch creates new shared persisted facts and changes how existing runtime paths fail, recover, and require operator action. It cannot be resolved safely as a mechanical contributor follow-up.

options.title: Sponsor the narrow durable boundary
options.body: Accept the residual shared-runtime direction and review the ordered series as a core architecture change with upgrade proof.

options.title: Narrow to owner-specific fixes
options.body: Reject shared recovery authority and request focused changes only in the existing lifecycle owners that have demonstrated gaps.

options.title: Pause the series
options.body: Defer the proposal until maintainers define a supported recovery product contract and ownership model.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the narrow durable boundary
recommendation.body: Accept the residual shared-runtime direction and review the ordered series as a core architecture change with upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The available evidence identifies this person as the author of the RFC and every linked implementation slice; a current-main owner should be added after maintainers identify the sponsoring area.
